attribution: Company-reported experimental results and reference methods transcribed from the latest Memory comparison table and the earlier consolidated evaluation report.
configuration: Results come from multiple source reports. Older rows include paper-reported references and company runs; matching models, samples and settings are not established. Compare only within the stated metric and subset; these are not a controlled cross-system reproduction.

systems.name: CoSens
systems.description: Experience layer with persistent memory and reusable methods. The reported memory implementation is named Friday in the source reports.
systems.evaluationNote: Company-run memory results. These scores do not evaluate the complete SDK or the Learn loop; a public evaluated source revision is not supplied.

systems.name: Mem0
systems.description: A memory layer that extracts, stores and retrieves information for agents and applications.
systems.evaluationNote: Latest-report rows use company-run Mem0 results; MemoryAgentBench explicitly uses Mem0 OSS. LoCoMo-Plus uses a paper reference. Platform, OSS and graph variants must not be treated as interchangeable.

systems.name: TencentDB Agent Memory
systems.description: TencentDB Agent Memory provides persistent memory infrastructure for agents.
systems.evaluationNote: Company-run results in the latest report. The exact evaluated release and storage configuration are not recorded; the current repository may differ from the evaluated version.

systems.name: A-Mem
systems.description: Agentic memory that organizes notes, metadata and links, and updates relationships as new memories arrive.
systems.evaluationNote: LoCoMo-Plus values are paper references reproduced in the company report. The system repository distinguishes the memory implementation from the authors’ experiment code.

systems.name: SeCom
systems.description: Conversation memory built from topical segments, with compression and retrieval over those memory units.
systems.evaluationNote: LoCoMo-Plus values are paper references reproduced in the company report; they are not a new controlled run of the current SeCom release.

systems.name: MemGPT
systems.description: The MemGPT agent design manages a limited context window using external memory and memory-editing tools.
systems.evaluationNote: MemBench uses the historical MemGPT reference from the source report. The current Letta project is its successor, not proof that this score measures today’s Letta release.

systems.name: RAG (local)
systems.description: The local retrieval-augmented memory baseline labeled ragmemory in the consolidated report.
systems.evaluationNote: A company-run baseline, not a separate publicly identified product. The report describes matched local conditions for its MemBench comparison but supplies no public implementation URL or complete configuration.

systems.name: Session RAG (V+fact)
systems.description: A LongMemEval paper reference using sessions as retrieval values, with session text and extracted facts as retrieval keys (K=V+fact).
systems.evaluationNote: The 86.2 value is the paper’s Table 3 retrieval reference transcribed into the company report. It is a method configuration, not an independently released memory product.

methodology.purpose: Tests whether an assistant can answer questions using information distributed across a long conversation history.
methodology.dataset: The public release contains ten multi-session conversations with timestamps, QA labels and evidence dialogue IDs.
methodology.procedure: Ingest conversation history, retrieve relevant memory for each question, generate an answer, then compare it with the annotated answer using the QA evaluator.
methodology.scoring: This row reports Overall Token-level F1 on a 0–1 scale: token precision and recall measure overlap with the reference answer. Higher is better; no LLM judge is needed for this selected metric.
methodology.scope: All three populated cells come from the latest company report. Sample selection, category inclusion, answer normalization and the exact Overall aggregation are not supplied; the repository’s full dataset size does not establish the company run size.

methodology.purpose: Tests hallucinations in memory extraction, memory updating and downstream question answering as separate operations.
methodology.dataset: HaluMem offers Medium and Long user-centric conversation histories, annotated memory points and QA pairs. This row selects Medium QA only.
methodology.procedure: Feed sessions through a memory-system adapter, collect stored and updated memories and QA predictions, then run the evaluation suite against annotated reference information.
methodology.scoring: Medium QA Correct is the reported correctness measure on a 0–1 scale. The official suite also evaluates memory extraction and update accuracy, hallucinations and omissions; those are not averaged into this row.
methodology.scope: The three values are company-run results in the latest report. Judge version, prompts, thresholds and evaluated QA count are not recorded. A high QA value alone does not establish extraction or update leadership.

methodology.purpose: Tests memory through incremental interactions, including accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding and conflict resolution.
methodology.dataset: The selected Conflict Resolution task provides facts that change or conflict across incoming context chunks.
methodology.procedure: Process chunks into memory in sequence, then answer questions that require the applicable updated fact rather than an outdated conflicting version.
methodology.scoring: MemoryAgentBench uses an adapted Token F1 in this company report, on a 0–1 scale. The official repository describes substring exact-match accuracy for its conflict-resolution tasks. These scoring protocols are different.
methodology.scope: Only Mem0 OSS and TencentDB have reported values; the CoSens result is missing. The adaptation code, chunk size, task revision, sample count and normalization rules are not supplied, so these values are not official-protocol accuracy.

methodology.purpose: Tests organizational memory: revised decisions, provenance, historical belief states, audit replay, justification chains and contradictions.
methodology.dataset: A synthetic organization with multiple authors, channels and valid-time versus ingestion-time history. The public Medium tier has 443 artifacts and 73 questions.
methodology.procedure: Ingest the selected tier with a system adapter, retrieve evidence, generate answers and judge them against structured rubric facets. The harness supports both native and shared answerers.
methodology.scoring: Overall rubric score is mean rubric-weighted facet coverage in [0,1], allowing partial credit. This row keeps the company report’s Medium result; its Small result is not mixed in.
methodology.scope: Only the CoSens company-run value is reported here. The public tier size describes the benchmark; actual evaluated question IDs, corpus revision, answerer, judge and run count are not supplied by the company report.

benchmarks.name: LongMemEval
benchmarks.source: Earlier consolidated report · retrieval evidence, not answer accuracy

methodology.purpose: Tests long-term interactive memory, including extraction, multi-session and temporal reasoning, knowledge updates and abstention.
methodology.dataset: Public S, M and oracle variants each contain 500 instances, with evidence session IDs and answer-bearing turn annotations. The company report does not identify its exact variant.
methodology.procedure: For retrieval evaluation, index the history, retrieve the ten highest-ranked memory items for each question, and check against annotated evidence. The benchmark separately supports generated-answer evaluation.
methodology.scoring: Evidence Recall@10 (%) measures reference evidence recovered in the top ten results, on a 0–100 scale. It is not end-to-end answer accuracy. The source does not provide the exact matching and aggregation implementation.
methodology.scope: CoSens is a company-run result; Session RAG (V+fact) is a Table 3 paper reference. Retrieval unit, evidence matching, embedding version, query expansion and sample selection are not established as matched.

benchmarks.name: LoCoMo-Plus
benchmarks.source: Earlier consolidated report · paper references and company result

links.title: Official code, data and judge framework

methodology.purpose: Adds cognitive memory to long conversational QA: use an earlier cue to respect a later implicit constraint, even when their wording differs.
methodology.dataset: Extends LoCoMo’s factual categories with cue–trigger cognitive tasks. This table selects the reported factual average, not the cognitive score or a combined total.
methodology.procedure: Build unified inputs, obtain predictions from the model or memory system, then score with the released LLM-as-judge framework.
methodology.scoring: The released judge awards correct, partial and wrong responses 1, 0.5 and 0. This row preserves the report’s factual average on a 0–100 scale; the company aggregation implementation is not supplied.
methodology.scope: CoSens is a company-run value. Mem0, A-Mem and SeCom are paper references copied into the consolidated report. Model, prompt, judge and exact sample equivalence have not been established.

benchmarks.name: MemBench
benchmarks.source: Earlier consolidated report · paper references and local baseline

methodology.purpose: Tests factual and reflective agent memory in participation and observation scenarios, with effectiveness, efficiency and capacity dimensions.
methodology.dataset: Participation data represents first-person interaction; observation data represents third-person information. Released data supports different conversation lengths and added distractor content.
methodology.procedure: Feed the chosen interaction history through a memory method, answer the associated questions and score correctness for the selected scenario and context-length condition.
methodology.scoring: This row uses reported Participation Scenario Accuracy on a 0–1 scale. Observation accuracy, efficiency and capacity are separate measures and are not combined into this value.
methodology.scope: CoSens and RAG (local) are company-run results; MemGPT is a paper reference. The report describes its local RAG comparison as matched, but exact lengths, question IDs, sample counts and scoring settings are not supplied.

selection: Use reported Overall scores where available; otherwise use the task-facing QA or answer-quality metric. Preserve the task and subset label. Missing results are null, displayed as —.
disclaimer: Experimental results are provided for reference only and do not constitute academic research. Results may be updated at any time as new evaluations become available.
